subject: Re: Kickoff: dual-pixel depth for the imaging pipeline
body:
Status.

Reproduction: done April 28. Kaia's runs of DPNet with affine invariance on the released train split land within 2% of the reference metrics on the test split across the board — consistent with the release notes saying the public dataset is slightly smaller than the paper's.

Affine-invariance investigation: as suspected, affine-ambiguous depth is fully sufficient for defocus but relighting needs metric-ish scale. Good news — using the camera's autofocus metadata as a weak anchor resolves the ambiguity well enough on 87% of our internal validation captures. I propose we scope relighting v1 to captures where the anchor is confident and fall back to defocus-only otherwise.

Risk: the distillation recipe's first student (May 8, two weeks ahead of plan — credit Linnea) is 14x smaller but loses more accuracy on the affine-invariant metrics than expected in the far-depth range. Next iteration weights the loss by inverse depth; if that doesn't close it, we may need a slightly larger student than the latency budget wants.

Fumiko
